# Draft:Teniola Zara King

is sourced to source 7 whynow. The "frequently explores" word usage is LLM, but it's not a fair rendition of the source material - disapora is mentioned in the headline and strap but not in the article.
Notability isn't provided either, since the sources are interviews or in-passing references. ChrysGalley (talk) 22:06, 4 January 2026 (UTC)}}
----
Teniola Zara King (born 8 July 1992) is a British-born film and television writer and director. She is best known for her short film Teju’s Tale, which was nominated for Best Short Film at the 9th Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) in 2023. King has also worked in television production in Nigeria and has served as a shadow director on British television dramas produced for Sky and Netflix.
Early life and education
King was born on 8 July 1992 in the United Kingdom and grew up between the UK and Lagos, Nigeria. She studied Economics at the University of Liverpool before beginning her professional career in television production in Nigeria.
She later returned to England to pursue formal film training and completed a Master of Arts in Filmmaking at the London Film School, where she developed her writing and directing skills through multiple short film projects.
Career
Television production in Nigeria
King began her career in the Nigerian television industry as a Production Assistant on Highlites With IK, one of Africa’s early late-night talk shows. Within several months, she was promoted to Line Producer, and later went on to serve as Series Producer on the M-Net television drama Head Over Heels.
Filmmaking and directing
After leaving television production to pursue filmmaking, King wrote and directed her first short film, Gidi High Life, which was filmed in Lagos and marked her transition into directing narrative cinema.
Her subsequent short film, Teju’s Tale (2022), was inspired by events from the 1950s and drew on her grandmother’s experiences as a Nigerian nurse arriving in the United Kingdom. The film explores themes of migration, identity, and racial discrimination within institutional settings. Teju’s Tale was nominated for Best Short Film at the 9th Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards in 2023.
Following the release of her short films, King served as a shadow director on the Sky Original drama The Midwich Cuckoos and on the Netflix drama Who Is Erin Carter?, produced by Left Bank Pictures.
Current work
King has been reported to be developing her debut television series, on which she is attached as both writer and director, in collaboration with DBK Studios and Sky Studios.
Style and themes
King’s work frequently explores diasporic experiences and historical narratives, particularly those relating to Black British and Nigerian identities. Her films often draw on personal and intergenerational stories to examine broader social themes.
Filmography
Short films
Gidi High Life – writer and director
Teju’s Tale (2022) – writer and director
Television
Highlites With IK – production assistant; line producer
Head Over Heels (M-Net) – series producer
The Midwich Cuckoos (Sky Original) – shadow director
Who Is Erin Carter? (Netflix) – shadow director
